response.title: Can the battery in a power station be replaced when it wears out, or do I have to buy a whole new one?
response.answer:
It depends on the brand and model. Some portable power stations have replaceable batteries, but many are sealed units where the manufacturer expects you to replace the entire power station when the battery wears out.

There are three common designs:

Type

	

Battery replacement

	

Examples




Sealed power stations

	

Usually not user-replaceable

	

Many Jackery, EcoFlow, and Bluetti models




Serviceable power stations

	

May be replaceable by the manufacturer or repair technician

	

Certain models, depending on parts availability




Modular power stations

	

Designed to add or swap battery modules

	

Some expandable power systems

How long do power station batteries last?

Most newer power stations use LiFePO4 (LFP) batteries, which last significantly longer than older lithium-ion batteries.

LiFePO4: Typically 3,000–4,000 charge cycles before dropping to around 80% capacity.

Older lithium-ion (NMC): Typically 500–1,000 cycles before reaching around 80% capacity.

For example, if you fully charge and discharge an LFP power station every day, 3,000 cycles translates to roughly 8 years.

Importantly, 80% capacity doesn't mean the battery is dead. It can continue working for years, just with reduced runtime.

What I recommend

If you're buying a power station and want to keep it for 10–15 years:

Choose LiFePO4 batteries.

Look for a model with officially replaceable battery modules.

Check whether the manufacturer sells replacement batteries, not just expansion batteries.

Check the warranty and repair policy.

One important distinction: An expandable battery system doesn't necessarily mean its original internal battery can be replaced.

Which power station are you considering?

Are you looking at EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti, Anker SOLIX, or another brand?

If you tell me the model, I can help determine whether its battery can actually be replaced, how much replacement might cost, and whether you'd need to buy a whole new unit.
